items.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
items.description: The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

items.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
items.description: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

items.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
items.description: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.

items.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
items.description: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

items.title: Flights and train services cancelled in Belgium due to strike
items.description: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.

items.title: Presidential villa suffers water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says
items.description: Bola Tinubu says he was shaving last week when the water cut out - an experience familiar to many Nigerians.

items.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
items.description: The couple have been together for four years and were engaged in 2025.

items.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
items.description: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".

items.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
items.description: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.

items.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
items.description: Choi Kyo-jin admits last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam caused chaos.

items.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
items.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

items.title: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
items.description: The Army says "swift action" is necessary to protect its personnel and nearby communities around its ammunition plant in Iowa.

items.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
items.description: At least three people were killed and many more feared dead after a fire at a confectionary factory.

items.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
items.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

items.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
items.description: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".

items.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.description: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

items.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
items.description: The hair was given as a sign of friendship shortly before Washington's death in 1799, according to a descendent of its former owner.

items.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
items.description: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

items.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
items.description: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.

items.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
items.description: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.
